summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: DNA is hydrophilic and negatively charged, requiring specialized methods to cross hydrophobic membranes: (1) Bacterial cells use CaCl2 divalent cations and 42°C heat shock; (2) Animal cells use Micro-injection; (3) Plant cells use Biolistics (Gene Gun) with DNA-coated gold/tungsten microprojectiles.

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 5.1 The Hydrophilic Barrier Problem
- DNA possesses a negatively charged sugar-phosphate backbone ($\text{PO}_4^{3-}$), making it a highly **hydrophilic polyanion**.
- Consequently, foreign DNA cannot cross the hydrophobic phospholipid bilayer of host plasma membranes without specialized physical or chemical permeabilization.

### 5.2 Bacterial Chemical Transformation ($\text{CaCl}_2$ + Heat Shock)
1. **Divalent Cation Incubation**: Bacterial cells (*E. coli*) are treated with ice-cold divalent calcium ions ($\text{Ca}^{2+}$ as $\text{CaCl}_2$). Positively charged $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ ions neutralize negative charges on both the outer membrane lipopolysaccharides and the DNA phosphate backbone, facilitating DNA adhesion to the cell surface.
2. **Thermal Pulse (Heat Shock)**: The cell-DNA mixture on ice ($0^\circ\text{C}$) is subjected to a transient thermal shock at **$42^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\text{--}90\text{ seconds}$**, and then returned immediately onto ice. This creates transient aqueous membrane pores through which the plasmid enters the bacterial cytoplasm.

### 5.3 Physical & Biological Gene Transfer Methods

| Transformation Method | Primary Target Host | Biophysical Mechanism & Equipment |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Chemical ($\text{Ca}^{2+}$ / Heat Shock)** | **Bacterial Cells** (*E. coli*) | Divalent cations mask negative charge; $42^\circ\text{C}$ heat pulse opens transient membrane pores |
| **Micro-Injection** | **Animal Cells** (e.g., fertilized oocyte) | Recombinant DNA is directly injected into the nucleus of an animal cell using an ultra-fine glass micropipette under an inverted microscope |
| **Biolistics / Gene Gun** | **Plant Cells** | Microscopic heavy metal particles (**Gold or Tungsten**, $1\ \mu\text{m}$) coated with foreign DNA are accelerated at supersonic velocities by helium pressure, penetrating the rigid cellulosic plant cell wall |
| **Electroporation** | Protoplasts / Mammalian cells | High-voltage electrical pulses ($1\text{--}2\text{ kV}$) transiently disrupt lipid bilayer orientation, opening reversible nanoscale pores |
| **Disarmed Pathogens** | Plants & Animals | *Agrobacterium tumefaciens* (plants) and disarmed retroviruses (animals) transfer foreign DNA naturally |

conceptBreakdown.heading: Lipofection (Liposome-Mediated Gene Transfer)
conceptBreakdown.title: Lipofection (Liposome-Mediated Gene Transfer)
conceptBreakdown.content: Cationic liposomes (e.g., Lipofectamine) encapsulate negatively charged plasmid DNA within artificial phospholipid vesicles that fuse spontaneously with mammalian plasma membranes to deliver recombinant constructs.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Protoplast Fusion via PEG
conceptBreakdown.title: Protoplast Fusion via PEG
conceptBreakdown.content: Plant cell walls are enzymatically removed to produce naked protoplasts, which are induced to fuse and take up foreign DNA in the presence of Polyethylene Glycol (PEG) and high calcium concentrations.
